subject: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)
body:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:15 AM PST
Subject: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

Hey Wei,

I want to lock the docs-site plan for model release notes this week so we can unblock the generator team (they need to know target URLs + what we’re calling the landing pages).

Proposed structure:

1) Nav + landing pages
- New top-level section: “Model release notes”
- Landing page: /models/release-notes
- Per-model landing: /models/<model_id>/release-notes
- Entries are date/version grouped and linkable (so Console can deep-link)

2) Feed
- JSON feed (primary) + RSS/Atom (nice-to-have but requested by customers)
- One global feed + per-model feed
- We should document how to subscribe + caching/ETag semantics at a high level (no internal implementation details)

3) Source
- Docs pages generated from the *published* changelog feed (not from git tags)
- “Published” means approval workflow has completed (draft -> in_review -> published)

Open questions for you:
- Do we want entries as separate docs pages (one page per release note) vs single page with anchors? My bias is single page per model (better UX + easier build).
- If we do RSS, should the item link go to the model landing page anchor (#event_id) or a dedicated entry page?

If you can reply with your recommendation today, I’ll incorporate into the PRD notes for DES-214 and leave comments on the redwood-docs PRs.

Attaching the latest IA sketch.

- Elliot

Attachment: model-release-notes-ia-v3.png (image/png)

---

From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

+1 to single page per model with anchors.

Reasons:
- RSS items can link to /models/<model_id>/release-notes#<event_id> (stable enough as long as we don’t reorder; event_id ordering should be deterministic)
- One page means fewer docs build artifacts and fewer chances for broken links in the Console
- Version/date filtering can be client-side in docs (or simple query param) without adding more routes

For the global landing page /models/release-notes:
- I’d do an index with recent entries (last 30 days) + search by model_id + link to per-model pages.

Re: feed formats:
- JSON feed is the canonical machine-readable artifact
- We can generate RSS/Atom from the same published JSON (as part of the docs build step)

One thing to be careful about: wording. We should make sure the template always includes a “Compatibility” block and never includes internal fields (e.g., vendor nicknames, internal benchmark IDs). I saw the linting idea mentioned in #995; that’s the right place to enforce.

If helpful, I can draft the “How to subscribe” docs page and a stub for the feed endpoint URLs.

- Wei

---

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 12:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

Perfect.

Let’s align on the exact endpoints/URLs we’ll commit to (since Console + SDKs will start linking soon):

Docs pages:
- /models/release-notes
- /models/{model_id}/release-notes

Feeds:
- /models/release-notes/feed.json
- /models/release-notes/feed.rss (or /feed.xml?)
- /models/{model_id}/release-notes/feed.json
- /models/{model_id}/release-notes/feed.rss

Do you have a preference for .rss vs .xml naming? I’m leaning .rss because it’s explicit and we can also add /feed.atom later.

On ordering: agreed on event_id. I’ll ping the platform team to confirm they’ve fixed “multiple updates in one day” ordering (I remember a staging bug).

Can you take a first pass at the subscription doc + endpoint naming today/tomorrow? I’ll start drafting the nav copy and add to PR #982.

Timeline proposal:
- Fri EOD: endpoint naming + doc stubs in a branch
- Mon/Tue: get review from me + a quick once-over from release eng (Connor) on freeze window wording
- End of next week: merge behind docs flag + ship RSS

- Elliot

---

From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

I prefer:
- /feed.json
- /feed.rss

…over /feed.xml since some customers explicitly asked for “RSS feed” and this avoids confusion.

I’ll draft:
1) “Subscribing to model release notes” page
- Explains global vs per-model feed
- Mentions that entries are published after review (so customers know it’s not real-time)
- Notes caching (ETag) at a conceptual level

2) A short “FAQ / troubleshooting” section
- “Why did I see a model behavior change before a note?” (answer: rollouts may precede docs sync by up to N hours; link to Console changelog as source of truth)

Quick question: do we want to call out update frequency as “daily batch” in docs? That’s accurate for v1 but might lock us in.

Attachment with initial endpoint/prose draft.

- Wei

Attachment: rss-feed-endpoints-proposal.md (text/markdown)

---

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 9:08 AM PST
Subject: Re: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

Great draft.

On frequency: let’s avoid “daily batch” phrasing. Suggest:
- “Published release notes are typically available within 24 hours of a model metadata change being approved.”

That gives us flexibility (and is still honest).

Also +1 on the FAQ. Please add a line that the Console changelog is the authoritative view for accounts that have access (docs site mirrors the published feed).

Review asks:
- Can you open a PR for the docs pages + feed endpoints naming today? Tag me + Kira if you want an enterprise-change-management wording sanity check (esp. in the FAQ).
- I’ll leave comments on #982 (nav + landing page) and #995 (linting rules). Once your PR is open we’ll cross-link.

We should make sure RSS items include:
- title: “{model_id} {version_id} — {change_type}”
- link: docs anchor
- guid: event_id
- pubDate: published_at (not the original update timestamp)

- Elliot

---

From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 4:42 PM PST
Subject: Re: Docs site: model release notes plan (nav + RSS)

PR is up: redwood-docs #1004 (RSS/Atom + subscription docs). Also added the endpoint naming and the “typically within 24 hours” wording.

Notes / things I’m unsure about (left as TODOs in the PR):
- Whether we should expose “Last updated” time on /models/release-notes (helps customers validate the docs mirror isn’t stale)
- If we want Atom now vs later (I put it behind a build flag but it’s easy to ship)

Can you review over the weekend / Monday morning? If we can land by Tue, that keeps us aligned with the changelog generator integration work (ENG-4926).

- Wei
